authorityStatus.limitationNotice: Authority corpus for live LOA verification is not yet wired; this guidance reflects design-only procedural patterns pending official authority confirmation.
controllingAuthorityNeeded: RMC No. 5-2026 or current LOA verification issuance
Relevant jurisprudence on LOA authority and due process

immediateSafeSteps: Identify LOA number, audit case number, taxable period, tax types, RO, GS, office, and signatory.
Submit available documents with transmittal and receiving proof.
Mark unavailable, non-applicable, or non-existent documents clearly.
Escalate to professional review for legal conclusions.
missingFacts: LOA number and audit case number
taxable period covered by the LOA
date of receipt of the LOA
confirmed scope of examination (tax types covered)
responsible revenue officer(s) and group supervisor names
taxable period covered by the notice
date of receipt of the notice
documentsNeeded: Certified true copy of the LOA
List of requested documents with availability status
riskWarnings: Avoid unnecessary admissions when responding to the LOA or during any related discussion with the examining office.
Failure to verify LOA authenticity or respond within the requested scope may weaken the taxpayer's procedural position.

workflowRecommendation.nextStep: Verify LOA authenticity and calendar the document submission deadline before responding.
prohibitedOverreach: Do not claim the LOA is invalid without authority verification.
Do not provide a final legal conclusion.

LOA_RECEIVED_WHAT_TO_DO.humanReviewNotice: This scaffold provides procedural-safe guidance only. authorityStatus.limitationNotice: Authority corpus for live verification of the scope of the termination letter is not yet wired; confirm the covered LOA, period, and tax types before relying on this guidance.
controllingAuthorityNeeded: Applicable RMO/RR on audit closure and reopening grounds
NIRC provisions on fraud, false returns, and refund-related exceptions

immediateSafeSteps: The audit case is closed for the covered LOA, tax period, and tax types, but the closure may be without prejudice to future action if fraud, false return, or refund-related issues later arise.
Match it to the LOA, audit case number, taxable period, and tax types.
Keep payment proof and BIR receipts.
Preserve transmittals, notices, returns, AFS, schedules, and prior correspondence.
Do not treat it as blanket immunity for unrelated periods, unrelated tax types, fraud, false returns, or refund issues.
missingFacts: exact LOA, audit case number, taxable period, and tax types covered by the termination letter
documentsNeeded: Prior transmittals, notices, returns, AFS, and schedules
riskWarnings: This closure is scoped to the covered LOA, period, and tax types only; it is not blanket protection against unrelated periods, unrelated tax types, fraud, false returns, or refund issues.

workflowRecommendation.nextStep: Match the termination letter to its covered LOA, period, and tax types, and retain all related records permanently.
prohibitedOverreach: Do not claim permanent, unconditional protection from every future BIR inquiry.
Do not claim the Bureau is permanently barred from revisiting related matters.
Do not provide a final legal conclusion.
